cases.title: Given names
cases.summary: Follow a path through repeated name entries.
cases.narrative: This invented patient excerpt contains two name entries, each with one or more given names.
cases.question: Which given names appear in the excerpt?
cases.explanation: The path flattens the given-name arrays into one collection in input order. It does not choose a preferred name.
edgeCases: A missing name or given field contributes no items.
Duplicate names remain duplicate items.

cases.title: First name
cases.summary: Index the first name entry, then read its given names.
cases.narrative: One name entry may contain several given names. Indexing a name entry does not select a single given name.
cases.question: What given names belong to the first name entry?
cases.explanation: Indexes are zero-based. The first name entry has two given names, so the result still has two items.
edgeCases: An out-of-range index returns an empty collection.
The result depends on the order recorded in this excerpt.

source.note: Original synthetic Callis preset; input, expression and expected result preserved.

cases.title: Filtered names
cases.summary: Select name entries by the recorded family value.
cases.narrative: The invented excerpt includes one family name. This example selects matching entries without deciding which name should be used.
cases.question: Which given names belong to an entry with family Example?
cases.explanation: where evaluates its criterion for each name entry, then the path reads the matching given names.
edgeCases: No matching entry produces an empty collection.
Multiple matching entries contribute their given names in order.

source.note: Original synthetic Callis preset; input, expression and expected result preserved.

cases.title: Name count
cases.summary: Count name entries rather than given-name strings.
cases.narrative: The two name entries in this invented excerpt contain three given-name strings altogether.
cases.question: How many name entries are present?
cases.explanation: count returns the number of items in its input collection. It does not count nested given-name values.
edgeCases: A missing name field counts as zero.
Duplicate entries count separately.

source.note: Original synthetic Callis preset; input, expression and expected result preserved.

cases.title: Has Ada
cases.summary: Check whether any name entry starts with Ada.
cases.narrative: This is a data-matching exercise on invented names, not an identity check.
cases.question: Does an entry have Ada as its first given name?
cases.explanation: exists returns one Boolean and stops when a matching name entry is found. It does not return the matching entry.
edgeCases: An empty name collection returns false.
Ada in a later given-name position would not match this criterion.

source.note: Original synthetic Callis preset; input, expression and expected result preserved.

cases.title: Filtered count
cases.narrative: This invented excerpt lets us distinguish the number of matching name entries from the number of matching strings.
cases.question: How many name entries have family Example?
cases.explanation: The filtered collection is passed to count. The result is a collection containing one Integer.
edgeCases: No matches returns [0], not an empty collection.
Every matching entry is counted, including duplicates.

cases.title: Missing field
cases.summary: Inspect an absent field without inventing a value.
cases.narrative: The excerpt intentionally contains no address field. It is not a complete patient record.
cases.question: What does the address path return for this excerpt?
cases.explanation: An absent path produces the empty collection. This says only that this JSON excerpt supplies no address; it says nothing about whether a person has an address.
edgeCases: A missing field and a field containing null contribute no items.
An empty collection is different from a collection containing false.

source.note: Original synthetic Callis preset; input, expression and expected result preserved.

cases.title: Boolean logic
cases.summary: Combine a recorded Boolean with a literal.
cases.narrative: The invented patient excerpt records active as true. This exercise shows Boolean evaluation, not a clinical status assessment.
cases.question: What is the result of active and true?
cases.explanation: The recorded true value and the true literal yield true under FHIRPath Boolean rules.
edgeCases: FHIRPath empty-collection logic is not JavaScript truthiness.
A missing active field must not be silently treated as false.

cases.title: Exact decimal
cases.summary: Preserve the text of a computed Decimal.
cases.narrative: This arithmetic example uses Decimal literals in the expression. It does not calculate a clinical recommendation from patient data.
cases.question: How is 0.1 plus 0.2 displayed?
cases.explanation: The playground requests decimalOutput string, so the computed Decimal is displayed as exact text. This is not a lossless JSON input parser.
edgeCases: Digits already lost by JSON.parse cannot be recovered.
A Decimal displayed as a string does not retain a distinct JavaScript type tag.

cases.title: Official given name
cases.summary: Select the name marked official in a synthetic excerpt.
cases.narrative: An invented patient excerpt records an official name and a nickname. The labels are recorded data; this example does not verify identity or choose a contact policy.
cases.question: Which given names are recorded under an official name?
cases.explanation: Filtering selects entries whose use is official, then reads their given names. Matching multiple entries returns a collection; this does not assert that only one official name is permitted.
edgeCases: No official name returns an empty collection.
Multiple official entries preserve their order and duplicates.

cases.title: Final observations
cases.summary: Count final Observation entries in a synthetic Bundle excerpt.
cases.narrative: This small invented Bundle contains one final Observation, one preliminary Observation and a Patient entry. It is a data-selection exercise, not an interpretation of any measurement.
cases.question: How many Observation resources in the excerpt have status final?
cases.explanation: The first filter keeps Observation resources; the second keeps the recorded final status. count returns their number. References are not resolved and the excerpt is not a validated complete Bundle.
edgeCases: No matching Observation returns [0].
Missing status is excluded; every matching entry counts, including duplicates.

cases.title: Phone entry
cases.summary: Check for a phone entry in a synthetic patient excerpt.
cases.narrative: The invented excerpt contains an email entry and no phone entry. Absence from this JSON does not establish whether a person has a phone number elsewhere.
cases.question: Does this JSON excerpt contain at least one phone entry?
cases.explanation: exists reports whether an entry has system phone. It does not validate a number, establish consent or decide whether contacting anyone is appropriate.
edgeCases: Missing or empty telecom returns false.
One or several phone entries return true; this criterion does not check their values.
